title: Mehrauli Archaeological Park Delhi - History & Travel Guide
content:
Mehrauli Archaeological Park - Hidden Heritage Treasure in Delhi,

Mehrauli Archaeological Park is one of Delhi’s most fascinating heritage sites, spread over 200 acres near the Qutub Minar complex. It is home to more than 100 ancient monuments, tombs, mosques, stepwells, and ruins that reflect Delhi’s long and layered history.

Walking through the park feels like stepping back in time. You will find the Jamali Kamali Mosque and Tomb, famous for its Indo-Islamic design, the Rajon Ki Baoli stepwell, known for its peaceful beauty, and many forgotten Mughal gardens and gateways. Each corner has a story to tell, dating back to different dynasties including the Tomars, Mughals, Lodhis, and the British.

Unlike other crowded tourist spots, Mehrauli Archaeological Park is calm and spacious, making it perfect for history lovers, photographers, and those who enjoy nature walks. Its mix of ruins, greenery, and old architecture makes it one of the best-kept secrets of Delhi.

The park is open daily from 5:00 AM to 6:30 PM, and entry is free for all visitors. The best time to explore is between October and March, when the weather is pleasant. Since it covers a large area, wearing comfortable shoes and carrying water is recommended.

Mehrauli Archaeological Park may not be as famous as the Red Fort or Humayun’s Tomb, but its hidden beauty and timeless charm make it a must-visit for anyone wanting to experience Delhi’s forgotten heritage.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: Nearest station is Qutub Minar (Yellow Line), about a 10-minute walk.
  • By Bus/Auto: Regular buses and autos from South Delhi’s main roads drop you nearby.
  • By Car: Limited parking near the Qutub Minar complex.

Entry Fee:

 Free for all visitors.

Travel Tip: Carry water and wear comfortable walking shoes - you’ll cover a lot of ground if you explore properly.
